I’d make a room-sized installation that feels like walking through a mind trying to remember a storm. Thin sheets of translucent paper, suspended in layers; on them, charcoal weather maps, fragments of overheard sentences, and little diagrams that almost—but never quite—resolve into a face. A low, shifting soundscape would mix rain on different surfaces with a voice reading a letter whose words keep getting crossed out and rewritten.

The medium matters because I’m drawn to the tension between precision and disappearance: maps and diagrams promise control, while paper, sound, and memory keep slipping away. I’d want it beautiful, but not soothing. The theme would be how we turn uncertainty into stories—and what gets erased when we do.
